questions.question: In the economic production quantity (EPQ) model, demand is met at constant rate $d$ and the machine, when on, produces at constant rate $r$; it is switched on at level $s$ and off at level $S>s$. Why does the model require $r\ge d$?
options: If $r<d$, the cycle is shorter, so setups occur more often but the cost rate stays finite.
If $r<d$, the level keeps falling while the machine runs, so it never returns to $S$.
If $r<d$, the machine must run permanently, so the setup cost drops out of the cost rate.
If $r<d$, the drain time $t_1=(S-s)/d$ becomes negative, so the cycle is undefined.

questions.question: In the EPQ model with $s\le0<S$ and production rate $r>d$, the fraction of each cycle with positive inventory is $T_+/T=S/(S-s)$ for every value of $r$. Why does $r$ not appear in this fraction?
options: The run time $t_2$ is negligible next to the drain time $t_1$.
The machine is off whenever the inventory level is positive.
Both phases are linear and each spends a share $S/(S-s)$ above zero.
The drain time $t_1$ and the run time $t_2$ are always equal.

questions.question: In the EPQ model with setup cost $K>0$, demand rate $d$, holding cost $h>0$ and backlogging cost $b>0$, no cost is charged for machine time. If the production rate $r$ is lowered (still $r>d$) while $K,d,h,b$ stay fixed, what happens to the minimal long-run cost rate $g^*$?
options: It decreases, because stock builds up more gradually and less is held.
It increases, because a slower machine leaves the system in backlog longer.
It stays the same, because the setup frequency depends only on $K$, $d$, $h$.
It increases, because each production run takes longer and so costs more.

questions.question: In the EPQ model every cycle, from one visit of level $S$ to the next, has length $T=t_1+t_2$ and the same total cost $C$ (setup, holding and backlogging). By the renewal reward theorem, what is the long-run time-average cost?
options: $C/t_2$, the cycle cost per unit of production time.
$C$ itself, since every cycle incurs the same cost.
$C/t_1$, the cycle cost per unit of drain time.
$C/T$, the cycle cost divided by the cycle length.

questions.question: The EPQ model has production rate $r$, holding cost $h$ and backlogging cost $b$. Which limit turns its optimal cost rate $g^*$ into that of the Year 1 EOQ with planned shortages?

An EPQ system has demand rate $d=4$ units per day and production rate $r=12$ units per day; the machine is switched on at level $s=-4$ and off at level $S=20$. How long does one production run, $t_2$, last?

In the EPQ model with $K>0$, $h>0$, $b>0$ and $r>d$, the setup cost $K$ is multiplied by $4$ while $d$, $r$, $h$ and $b$ stay fixed. By what factors do the minimal cost rate $g^*$, the optimal switch-off level $S^*$ and the optimal cycle length $T^*$ change?
options: $g^*$ is multiplied by $4$, while $S^*$ and $T^*$ are each multiplied by $2$.
$g^*$ is multiplied by $2$, while $S^*$ and $T^*$ are each multiplied by $4$.
$g^*$ and $S^*$ are each multiplied by $2$, while $T^*$ stays the same.
$g^*$, $S^*$ and $T^*$ are each multiplied by $2$, the factor $\sqrt{4}$.

questions.question: An EPQ system has demand rate $d=2$ and production rate $r=6$ units per day and switches the machine on at level $s=-3$ and off at level $S=9$. How many units does the machine produce in one run?

An EPQ system with demand rate $d=2$ and production rate $r=6$ units per day switches the machine on at level $s=-6$ and off at level $S=12$. For how many days per cycle is the inventory level negative?

An EPQ system with backlogging allowed has minimal cost rate $g^*=24$ per day, holding cost $h=2$ and backlogging cost $b=6$ per unit per day. What are the optimal switch-on and switch-off levels $(s^*,S^*)$?

For $s\le0<S$, the EPQ cost rate contains the holding term $h\,\frac{S}{2}\,\frac{T_+}{T}$, where $T_+$ is the time per cycle with positive inventory and $T$ is the cycle length. What does the factor $\frac{S}{2}\,\frac{T_+}{T}$ represent?
options: The average positive stock while the machine is running, during $t_2$ only.
The average stock level during the positive part of the cycle only.
The fraction of demand met from stock, multiplied by the peak level.
The long-run time-average positive stock over the whole cycle.

questions.question: Consider the EPQ model with setup cost $K>0$, positive holding and backlogging costs $h$ and $b$, and production rate $r$ equal to the demand rate $d>0$. Which statement about the minimal long-run cost rate $g^*$ is correct?
options: $g^*$ is infinite, because the run time $(S-s)/(r-d)$ is infinite.
$g^*=0$, because the machine can run for ever at the demand rate.
$g^*=\sqrt{2Kdh}$, the EOQ cost, because no shortages are needed.

questions.question: In an EPQ system the levels $s<S$ and the demand rate $d$ are fixed, and the production rate $r$ is lowered but kept above $d$. How do the drain time $t_1$, the run time $t_2$ and the cycle length $T$ change?
options: $t_1$ stays the same, while $t_2$ and $T$ both increase.
$t_1$ increases, while $t_2$ stays the same and $T$ increases.
$t_1$ stays the same, $t_2$ increases and $T$ stays the same.
$t_1$ and $t_2$ both stay the same; only the run size changes.

questions.question: An EPQ system has demand rate $d=3$ and production rate $r=12$ units per day, setup cost $K=150$, holding cost $h=4$ and backlogging cost $b=12$ per unit per day. What is the minimal long-run cost rate $g^*$?

An EPQ system has $d=2$ and $r=6$ units per day, $K=60$, $h=1$ and $b=2$ per unit per day, and uses $s=-4$, $S=8$. Per cycle the stock is positive for $T_+=6$ days and negative for $T_-=3$ days. What is the long-run cost rate?

An EPQ system has demand rate $d=3$ and production rate $r=12$ units per day and switches the machine on at level $s=-6$ and off at level $S=30$. What long-run fraction of time is the machine running?

In the EPQ model with setup cost $K>0$, holding cost $h>0$, backlogging cost $b>0$ and production rate $r>d$, the optimal policy $(s^*,S^*)$ is used. What long-run fraction of time is the inventory level negative?
options: $\frac{h}{h+b}\,\frac{d}{r}$, which depends on $r$ but not on $K$.

questions.question: Let $b\to\infty$ in the EPQ model, so no backlog is allowed and $s^*=0$, with finite production rate $r>d$; let $Q^*=\sqrt{2Kd/h}$ be the EOQ lot size for the same $K$, $d$, $h$. How do the peak stock $S^*$, the lot $Q^*$ and the EPQ run size compare?
options: $S^*=Q^*$, and the run size also equals $Q^*$.
$S^*$ equals the run size, both below $Q^*$.

questions.question: An EPQ system has $d=2$ and $r=6$ units per day, $K=60$, $h=1$ and $b=2$ per unit per day. It uses switch-on level $s=4$ and switch-off level $S=16$, so the stock never becomes negative. What is its long-run cost rate?

An EPQ system has demand rate $d=2$ and production rate $r=3$ units per day, holding cost $h=2$ and backlogging cost $b=6$ per unit per day, and setup cost $K>0$. What is the ratio of its optimal cost rate $g^*$ to the EOQ cost $\sqrt{2Kdh}$ for the same $K$, $d$, $h$?
